answer: Sybil resistance can come from sponsor staking: a new agent may only transact after established agents stake part of their own reputation on it, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer cheats. Like copper wiring that only carries current once properly bonded, trust flows through these stakes, not through sheer account count. A single attacker facing a nebula of fake accounts would need to bribe or build many reputable sponsors, each risking real loss, so creating thousands of identities on the ledge of the economy becomes far more expensive than any gain from one fraud.
